Indonesian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Malay sedia, from Sanskrit साध्य (sādhya).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /səˈdia/ [səˈdi.a]
  • Rhymes: -a
  • Syllabification: se‧di‧a

Adverb

[edit]

sêdia

  1. (archaic or poetic) as it has always been; from the beginning; as it was from the start
    Synonyms: selalu, sejak semula, sedari dulu, dari dulu
  2. (archaic or poetic) truly; indeed
    Synonyms: benar-benar, sebenarnya, memang

Derived terms

[edit]
  • sedianya

Verb

[edit]

sêdia

  1. to be finished
    Synonym: jadi
  2. to be ready
    Synonyms: mustaid, siap
  3. to be willing
    Synonyms: mau, sanggup
  4. to be present; available
    Synonym: ada
  5. synonym of sudah, telah

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bersedia
  • bersedia-sedia
  • kesediaan
  • ketersediaan
  • mempersediakan
  • menyediakan
  • penyedia
  • penyediaan
  • persediaan
  • sediaan
  • tersedia

Further reading

[edit]
  • “sedia”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016

Interlingua

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈse.dja/

Noun

[edit]

sedia (plural sedias)

  1. (item of furniture) chair
  2. seat

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From sedere.

The initial auto-gemination found in some regional Italian varieties seems to be unetymological.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsɛ.dja/[1][2], (regional) */ˈsɛ.dja/[2]
    • Rhymes: -ɛdja
    • Hyphenation: sè‧dia
  • (regional) IPA(key): /ˈse.dja/
    • Audio (una sedia):(file)
    • Rhymes: -edja
    • Hyphenation: sé‧dia

Noun

[edit]

sedia f (plural sedie)

  1. (furniture) chair
    Synonym: seggiola

Derived terms

[edit]
  • sedia a dondolo (“rocking chair, rocker”)
  • sedia a rotelle (“wheelchair”)
  • sedia a sdraio (“deck chair / deckchair”)
  • sedia elettrica (“electric chair”)
  • sediaio

Related terms

[edit]
  • sedere
  • sediario
  • seduta
  • seggio

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Ottoman Turkish: سدیه (sedye)
    • → Turkish: sedye

See also

[edit]
  • poltrona (“armchair”)

References

[edit]
  1. ^ sedia in Bruno Migliorini et al., Dizionario d'ortografia e di pronunzia, Rai Eri, 2025
  2. ↑ 2.0 2.1 sedia in Luciano Canepari, Dizionario di Pronuncia Italiana (DiPI)

Anagrams

[edit]
  • adesi, desia, diesa, sedai, sieda

Malay

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Sanskrit साध्य (sādhya).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /sədia/
  • Rhymes: -dia, -ia, -a

Adverb

[edit]

sedia (Jawi spelling سديا)

  1. from the beginning; in the beginning
    Synonyms: asal, dahulu, semula
  2. actually, indeed.
    Synonyms: benar-benar, sebenarnya, memang
    Yang hidup sedia akan mati juga sudahnya.
    Those who live will indeed one day die.
  3. already
    Synonym: sudah
    Alia sedia mengetahui soalan apa yang akan ditanyakan dalam ujian.
    Alia already knew what kind of questions will be asked in the test.

Adjective

[edit]

sedia (Jawi spelling سديا, comparative lebih sedia, superlative paling sedia)

  1. ready, prepared
    Synonyms: siap, mustaid, lengkap
    Kami sedia untuk menjawab kertas ujian pertama.
    We are ready to answer the first exam paper.
  2. willing, eager
    Synonyms: sanggup, rela, sudi
    Antonym: enggan
    Jepun sedia menghantar batuan ke negara yang tersekutu dengannya.
    Japan is willing to send help to its allied countries.
  3. present, available
    Synonyms: ada, terdapat, wujud
    Antonym: tiada
    Asalnya, di kelab Inggeris, sedia 30 ahli.
    In the beginning, there were 30 members in the English club.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bersedia
  • disediakan
  • kesediaan
  • menyediakan
  • penyediaan
  • persediaan
  • sediakan
  • sedianya
  • siap sedia
  • tersedia

Interjection

[edit]

sedia (Jawi spelling سديا)

  1. (military) Used as a command to bring soldiers to the attention position
    Synonym: siap (Indonesian)

Descendants

[edit]
  • > Indonesian: sedia (inherited)
  • → Tausug: saddiya

[edit]
